title: Bassoon
summary: Limits first: one corner of the grid sounds and it is not a D2 note; the first render and the other three corners are exactly silent. No page of this instrument is posted. A first render of D2 on a labelled assembly of three sources plays nothing at the first printed pressures: from 0.6 s to 2.3 s the clip is exactly zero (attack 0.15 to 0.6 s: rms 1.63e-3 Pa, peak 0.0189 Pa; blowing 1961 Pa, 0.206 of the reed's 9.5 kPa closing pressure). The assembly: the Heckel1-O-Murry body (Johann Adam Heckel, 18 keys, c. 1840-50, Murry Collection; Hichwa-Rachor database sheets, list v48 of 7 March 2025; numbers only, no sheet committed) with 23 tone holes on a 2382.7 mm unfolded column; the bocal of a Grenser bassoon (Historisches Museum Basel 1904.312), another maker and date, whose two printed end diameters (4.2 and 9.8 mm) carry a straight cone declared here; and the reed numbers of one plastic Selmer 270M reed in an artificial mouth (Grothe 2014, Table 3.2). It is a stand-in: not the instrument of the Iowa recordings, whose system is not known, and not a modern bassoon. A 2 x 2 grid of printed values followed (closing pressure 9.5 kPa, the structural curve, or 7.1 kPa, the flow fit of the same table; blowing pressure 1961 Pa mf, the mean of the up and down rows of Bn1, or 2648 Pa ff, the up row of Bn1 alone; Fuks and Sundberg 1996). 9.5 kPa with 1961 Pa, 7.1 kPa with 1961 Pa (ratio 0.276) and 9.5 kPa with 2648 Pa (ratio 0.279) are silent: exactly zero from 0.6 s to 2.3 s, attack rms 1.63e-3, 1.61e-3 and 1.94e-3 Pa. 7.1 kPa with 2648 Pa (ratio 0.373) sounds, 1.89 Pa rms from 0.6 s to 2.3 s, steady, peak 8.60 Pa, nothing clipped, but it is not periodic: the autocorrelation peak is 0.746 where the criterion fixed before the run asked 0.9 for a note. Its spectral lines are 158.25 Hz and its multiples and 74.98 Hz + k x 158.25 Hz (k = 0 to 3); the 74.98 Hz line is 36 cents above D2 (73.42 Hz) and 22.6 dB under the strongest line (549.7 Hz). All four clips are one binary (music_render build b6g, md5 3177812b24a7) and one card but for the named values.
physics_present: the Heckel1-O-Murry air column as a numbers-only table, each row citing its Hichwa-Rachor sheet row: 23 rod-station diameters, 23 tone holes with diameter, depth and distance (the keyed holes from the General Information sheet), the two bores and the U-turn of the boot, the long joint and bell lengths and the receiver choke; the pitch of 440 Hz is the database authors' program input; the wing and boot heights sum to 849.9 mm against the printed 832 mm, 17.9 mm unreconciled (about 13 cents)

the bocal of another instrument (Grenser H3, sheet rows 2 to 6): 4.2 mm at the reed end, 9.8 mm at the wing end (equal to the Heckel1 receiver bore), string 33.3 mm, metal 334 and 314 mm; a straight cone between the two end diameters is DECLARED (the sheet prints no profile): 4.2 mm to 9.224 mm over 290.7 mm, then a 0.576 mm step to the 9.8 mm receiver

the reed numbers of Grothe's Table 3.2, structural column, mapped to the lumped single-reed owner: rest opening 1 mm, width 9.3 mm, closing pressure 9.5 kPa (flow fit 7.1 kPa), stiffness 494 N/m, mass 7.28e-6 kg, damping ratio 0.1163; the face area the engine implies (stiffness over closing pressure times rest opening) is 52 mm2 against the printed S_r of 26 mm2, and Grothe gives S_r and Q_r only to a factor 2

Fuks and Sundberg 1996 blowing pressures of player Bn1 at D2, kept as player data: mf 1961 Pa (mean of up 21 and down 19 cm H2O) and ff 2648 Pa (up row, 27 cm H2O; the mean of the two ff rows would be 2550 Pa)

the D2 fingering, tone holes 20, 22 and 23 counted from the reed end open and all others closed, read from Almenraeder 1824 Tabelle II, a 15-key chart of another instrument used as a DECLARED stand-in: the plate prints no legend (filled = closed is inferred from its first column), the D2 column's second row is a smudged outline read as open, the row-to-hole identity is probable, and holes with no plate row take the closed rest state by declaration

generic fs-duct conical and cylindrical segments, tone-hole side branches, a flanged bell load, the lumped single-reed owner and the physical baffled outlet receiver already run for the clarinet, now given this geometry in four renders (the exhaled-breath gas pack, 20 C dry room air, 2.65 s)

numerical settings, not measurements: a 48 kHz mechanics clock (the oboe's 96 kHz made the characteristic-line ladder of this 2.38 m bore refuse), a line_ladder row of 1e-10 and 131072 taps; a passive-sweep check planned for this card was dropped, the n3d build (md5 650c26c00a2c) printing no impedance lines for these cards, so no sweep could be read (its unplanned renders of s1, s2 and d2 were silent, rms 9.6e-4, 8.8e-4 and 6.8e-4 Pa)
physics_missing: a note: C3 and every pitch but D2 are not built; C3's plate column needs the chart's right-hand table, whose rows r10 and r11 are keys of unidentified holes; no fingering chart is printed for the Heckel1; the all-holes-closed and bell-hole-open states were not rendered

a clean oscillation at the printed values: three of the four corners are silent and the fourth is quasi-periodic (two lines, 74.98 Hz and 158.25 Hz, with their sums); the reed numbers are one plastic reed's in an artificial mouth on modern bocals, not a cane reed of the 1840s
a player: one fixed blowing pressure of one modern player (Bn1), no lip or embouchure row, no tongue, no vocal tract; no blowing pressure measured on a bassoon of the 1840s
pad lift and key rise (the sheets give none), tone-hole undercut and edge rounding (the sheet notes undercutting), chimney heights (the sheet's depth readings stand in)
the bocal's measured profile (only its two end diameters are printed) and the 17.9 mm of the wing and boot heights
the reference of the keyed holes' distances (near edge or centre; not stated), and the low Eb and low C# 'from the small tenon', read from the bottom tenon, an assumption
the instrument of the Iowa recordings, the comparison target: its system, maker and pitch are not known
blocked: C3 and every further pitch: the Almenraeder plate's right-hand table has keys of unidentified holes (rows r10 and r11) and no fingering chart is printed for the Heckel1; needs the instrument's own chart or an identification of those keys. D2 at a clean note: not reached at the printed values; a reed or an embouchure number outside the printed ones was not run (the grid was limited to printed values).
